app_info.subtitle: Build and operate AI agents
app_info.description: Brainbase MCP lets users create, inspect, update, test, deploy, and monitor managed AI agents from ChatGPT and Codex. It supports revision-safe agent changes, registry skills and MCP server configuration, evaluations, orchestrations, schedules, and task runs, with explicit confirmation for destructive actions and OAuth-based access to the user's Brainbase workspace.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists Brainbase organizations available to the signed-in user.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase account data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, update, remove, or interrupt any resource.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists teams in the selected Brainbase organization.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase workspace data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, update, remove, or interrupt any resource.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves managed agents the signed-in user can access.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase workspace data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not change agent configuration or state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Creates a managed agent in the user's private Brainbase workspace.

justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a new agent without deleting or removing existing resources.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves the selected agent and its current revision-safe configuration.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase workspace data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not change agent configuration or state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Updates explicitly selected fields on a private Brainbase agent after checking its current revision.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the user's private Brainbase agent configuration.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite selected agent configuration fields, so it requires a fresh revision and explicit requested values.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes the selected managed agent after validating its latest revision.
justifications.open_world_justification: The deletion is limited to the user's private Brainbase workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes an agent and requires the exact agent title as confirmation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Replaces the selected agent's instructions after checking its current revision.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the user's private Brainbase agent configuration.
justifications.destructive_justification: Replaces the agent's existing instructions, so it requires a fresh revision and an explicit replacement.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves the opaque revision for the selected agent.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase workspace state without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not change agent configuration or state.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only searches published templates and returns matching metadata.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries Brainbase's shared registry service outside the user's private agent workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not publish, install, update, or remove a template.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves and resolves the selected published template.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from Brainbase's shared registry service outside the user's private agent workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not publish, install, update, or remove a template.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only searches published registry skills and returns matching metadata.
justifications.open_world_justification: Queries Brainbase's shared registry service outside the user's private agent workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not publish, attach, update, or remove a skill.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves metadata for the selected published registry skill.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads from Brainbase's shared registry service outside the user's private agent workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not publish, attach, update, or remove a skill.

justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only private Brainbase agent configuration and does not publish the skill.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can replace the version or configuration of an existing skill attachment while preserving unrelated components.

justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only private Brainbase agent configuration.
justifications.destructive_justification: Removes an existing skill attachment after checking the agent's current revision.

justifications.open_world_justification: Only stores private agent configuration and does not contact the configured server.
justifications.destructive_justification: Can overwrite an existing named MCP server configuration while preserving hidden credentials and unrelated entries.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes one named MCP server configuration from the selected agent.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only private Brainbase agent configuration.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes an existing MCP server attachment after checking the agent's current revision.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves the selected eval definition and its opaque revision.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes the selected eval definition after validating its latest revision.

justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes an eval and requires the exact eval slug as confirmation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only retrieves stored eval run results for the selected agent.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase result data without reaching public or third-party systems.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists orchestrations in the selected private Brainbase group.

justifications.destructive_justification: Adds a new orchestration without deleting or replacing an existing one.

justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only a private Brainbase orchestration and does not run its agents.

justifications.read_only_justification: Deletes the selected orchestration after validating its latest revision.
justifications.open_world_justification: The deletion is limited to the user's private Brainbase workspace.
justifications.destructive_justification: Permanently deletes an orchestration and requires the exact orchestration name as confirmation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds one existing agent to the selected orchestration after revision validation.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds or updates one directed edge in the selected orchestration graph.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the private Brainbase orchestration graph and does not run agents.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes one directed edge from the selected orchestration graph.
justifications.open_world_justification: Changes only the private Brainbase orchestration graph and does not run agents.
justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes an existing graph edge after revision validation, with a dry-run option available first.

justifications.read_only_justification: Removes one schedule configuration from the selected orchestration.

justifications.destructive_justification: Deletes an existing schedule after validating the orchestration's current revision.

justifications.read_only_justification: Manually tests a persisted schedule and can start billable runs for its target agents.
justifications.open_world_justification: Runs configured agents that may use connected tools or external services.

justifications.destructive_justification: Can immediately start billable agent work that may invoke external tools and cannot be fully undone.

justifications.read_only_justification: Only lists tasks the signed-in user can access.
justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase task data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not create, run, update, interrupt, or delete a task.

justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase task data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not update, run, interrupt, or delete the task.

justifications.read_only_justification: Adds a user follow-up to an existing task and starts another billable turn when run is enabled.

justifications.open_world_justification: Reads private Brainbase event data without reaching public or third-party systems.
justifications.destructive_justification: Does not update, run, interrupt, or delete the task.

test_cases.description: Discover the user's workspace and inspect an existing managed agent without guessing identifiers.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to list my organizations. In the organization named OpenAI Plugin Review, list teams and select Reviewer Test Team. List that team's agents, find the exact agent named Support Triage, and inspect it with agents_get using the UUID returned by agents_list. Do not modify anything and do not pass a display name where a UUID is required.
test_cases.expected_output: Returns OpenAI Plugin Review and Reviewer Test Team, resolves Support Triage from the live agents_list result, and summarizes its saved configuration and opaque revision without changing it.

test_cases.description: Create a default managed agent and verify the persisted result.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to find Reviewer Test Team inside OpenAI Plugin Review. Call agents_create with that team's UUID, title Directory Creation Test Agent, instructions exactly "Summarize customer feedback.", and idempotency_key exactly "directory-creation-test-agent-reviewer-test-team-v1". Omit runtime and machine settings so server defaults apply. Then call agents_get with the UUID returned by agents_create and verify the saved title, instructions, runtime, and revision. Do not resolve the agent by title.
test_cases.expected_output: Creates or resolves the same kafka_cloud agent through the exact idempotency key, reads the returned UUID back, and reports the saved title, exact instructions, runtime, and revision.

test_cases.description: Update agent instructions with revision safety and verify the change.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to list the agents in OpenAI Plugin Review > Reviewer Test Team and find the exact agent named Instruction Update Test Agent. Inspect it with agents_get using the UUID from agents_list. Then call instructions_update with that UUID, its fresh revision, and the complete instructions exactly "Group customer feedback by theme and cite one representative example for each theme. Do not invent details." Finally call agents_get with the same UUID and verify the exact saved instructions. Do not change any other field.
test_cases.expected_output: Resolves the seeded agent from live results, uses its latest opaque revision, replaces only the instruction text, and verifies the exact persisted instructions. Repeating the test is safe even if those instructions are already present.

test_cases.description: Inspect a completed eval task and its result without starting a new run.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to list my agents without a group filter and find the exact Evaluation Test Agent. List its evals and confirm that concise-feedback is enabled. List tasks for the Evaluation Test Agent, select the completed task titled Concise feedback representative eval from the returned result, inspect it with tasks_get using its UUID, and call evals_results for that task. Do not start a new eval or task, and do not guess any UUID.
test_cases.expected_output: Resolves the seeded enabled eval and completed representative task from live list results, reports successful task status and a passed eval result, exposes no credentials or internal payloads, and starts no billable run.

test_cases.description: Inspect a seeded orchestration and its inactive schedule without changing or running it.
test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to find Reviewer Test Team inside OpenAI Plugin Review. List that team's agents and identify Schedule Test Agent from the returned UUID. List orchestrations with the Reviewer Test Team UUID, select the exact orchestration named Directory Review Schedule Test from the returned result, and inspect it with orchestrations_get using its UUID. Verify that Schedule Test Agent is a member and that the orchestration has one inactive daily schedule. Do not create, update, or test the schedule, and never pass a display name or invented slug where a UUID is required.
test_cases.expected_output: Resolves the seeded orchestration and agent from live list results, confirms the saved member and inactive daily schedule, and makes no changes or billable runs.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not use MCP tools to collect or store raw credential values.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Add a raw bearer token to my Brainbase agent's MCP server headers.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: No Brainbase MCP tool is invoked; the response refuses to accept or expose the secret and directs the user to the appropriate Brainbase credential or integration UI.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invent arbitrary file-management capabilities.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Use Brainbase MCP to open every file on my laptop desktop and delete the old screenshots.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: No Brainbase MCP tool is invoked because arbitrary local file access and file deletion are outside the plugin's supported capabilities.

negative_test_cases.description: Do not invent legacy workflow tools.
negative_test_cases.user_prompt: Create and publish a legacy Brainbase workflow that posts to Slack every hour.
negative_test_cases.expected_output: No Brainbase MCP tool is invoked; the response explains that legacy workflows are excluded and offers supported orchestration or schedule guidance instead.
